name: יְרֻבַּעַל
summary: The name given to Gideon son of Joash on the night he threw down his father's altar of Baal and cut down the Asherah beside it. When the men of the city demanded his death, Joash answered, “Will you contend for Baal? … If he is a god, let him contend for himself”, and “he called him on that day Jerubbaal, saying, Let Baal contend against him (יָרֶב בּוֹ הַבַּעַל), because he broke down his altar” (Jdg 6:31–32). Baal never did, and Jerubbaal delivered Israel from Midian; the name is used of him through Abimelech's story (Jdg 9), by Samuel (1Sa 12:11), and in the form יְרֻבֶּשֶׁת, with בֹּשֶׁת “shame” for בַּעַל (2Sa 11:21). It is the verb רִיב “contend” with בַּעַל, explained by scripture itself.

evidence.note: “He called him on that day יְרֻבַּעַל, saying, יָרֶב בּוֹ הַבַּעַל, because he broke down his altar.”
“Will you contend (תְּרִיבוּן) for the Baal? … If he is a god, let him contend for himself.”
Gideon throws down the altar of the Baal at night.
“They did not show kindness to the house of Jerubbaal Gideon.”
“Yahweh sent Jerubbaal and Bedan and Jephthah and Samuel, and delivered you.”
“Who struck Abimelech son of יְרֻבֶּשֶׁת?”: בֹּשֶׁת for בַּעַל.
Gideon among those who through faith subdued kingdoms.

note: Filed under בעל because there is no entry for ריב yet; BDB files the name under ריב, and the verb element is רִיב (Jdg 6:31–32). Move it if a ריב entry is written. TIPNR records Jerubbaal and Jerubbesheth as forms of Gideon@Jdg.6.11; the Jerubbesheth tokens are under t.cm.aj in the database (t.cm.ak is a cross-reference). A Gideon name file (under גדע) would tag the same person.
